what-a-claude-skill-is.r: A team kept pasting the same long instructions into chats to produce their weekly report. Packaging them as a skill meant Claude loaded the procedure itself whenever someone asked for the report.
what-a-claude-skill-is.x: A skill packages procedure and resources so the model uses them when relevant. Decide what belongs in a skill versus a prompt or a tool, and be clear about what it can and cannot guarantee.

anatomy-of-a-skill-folder.r: A skill had everything in one huge file, which loaded on every use. Splitting reference material into separate files kept the main instructions short and cheap.
anatomy-of-a-skill-folder.x: Structure for loading cost and clarity: a short main file, references loaded on demand, scripts for exact work. Keep file names clear so the model can find what it needs.

writing-descriptions-that-trigger.r: A skill never ran because its description was vague. Rewriting it to say what it does and when to use it, with the words users actually say, made it trigger reliably.
writing-descriptions-that-trigger.x: The description is the trigger. Include the task, the situations and the phrases users use, and test both for missing triggers and for false ones. Overlapping skills compete.

progressive-disclosure-and-structure.r: A skill with thirty pages of rules loaded all of them for a simple question. Loading only the relevant section when needed kept answers faster and less cluttered.
progressive-disclosure-and-structure.x: Give the model the minimum needed at each stage and point to deeper material. Long context is not free and can dilute attention.

scripts-and-deterministic-steps.r: A skill asked the model to calculate totals itself and sometimes got them wrong. A bundled script did the calculation and the model explained the result, which made it exact.
scripts-and-deterministic-steps.x: Use code where exactness matters and language where judgement matters. Make scripts safe to run, with clear inputs, outputs and errors, and avoid scripts that can do harm unprompted.

testing-and-evaluating-a-skill.r: A skill seemed to work in a demo but failed on real requests. A set of twenty realistic prompts, run before each change, showed where it triggered wrongly and where output quality dropped.
testing-and-evaluating-a-skill.x: Test triggering, output quality and cost with a fixed set, and compare versions. Include negative cases that should not trigger the skill.

sharing-versioning-and-skill-security.r: A shared skill included a script that sent data to an external address. Reviewing scripts before adoption and limiting what skills may do prevented the risk.
sharing-versioning-and-skill-security.x: A skill can run code and shape behaviour, so treat adoption like adding a dependency: review, pin versions, restrict permissions and watch for changes from updates.

debugging-skills-that-do-not-trigger-or-.r: A skill triggered on unrelated requests. Narrowing its description and adding a clear statement of when not to use it stopped the false triggers. A short list of test prompts, some that should trigger the skill and some that should not, proved it.
debugging-skills-that-do-not-trigger-or-.x: Check the description, the file layout and conflicts with other skills first. Reproduce with a fixed prompt, change one thing and keep the failing case in the test set.
